questions.question: Which dance of Eastern India was recognized in the Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2010?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Chhau**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chhau** is a traditional dance form from **Eastern India**, primarily performed in the states of **Odisha, Jharkhand, and West Bengal**.
 
• The dance is recognized by **UNESCO** as an element of the **Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity** in the year **2010**.
 
• It is a unique dance form that combines elements of **martial arts, tribal traditions, and folk culture**.
 
• Chhau dance is performed during major festivals, especially during **Chaitra Parva**, which is celebrated in the month of April.
 
• The dance is known for its elaborate **masks** (used in Purulia Chhau) and vibrant **costumes**, which depict characters from Hindu epics like the **Ramayana and Mahabharata**.
 
• There are three distinct styles of Chhau dance: **Purulia Chhau (West Bengal), Seraikella Chhau (Jharkhand), and Mayurbhanj Chhau (Odisha)**, each with its own unique characteristics.
 
• The dance is often accompanied by traditional **folk music** played on instruments like the **dhol, dhamsa, and shehnai**.
 
• Chhau is not just a cultural expression but also a means of storytelling that conveys **mythological tales** and local folklore.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Garba**__

 __
 
• **Garba** is a popular dance form from the state of **Gujarat**, performed during the festival of **Navratri**.
 
• It is primarily a **community dance** where participants move in a circular formation around an earthen lamp or a picture of a deity.
 
• The dance is accompanied by traditional **Gujarati folk songs** and rhythmic clapping.
 
 
 
• **Bihu**__
 __
 
• **Bihu** is a traditional dance form of **Assam**, performed during the **Bohag Bihu festival**, which marks the Assamese New Year.
 
• The dance is known for its **energetic movements** and vibrant **costumes**.
 
• It is accompanied by traditional Assamese instruments like the **dhol, pepa, and gogona**.
 
 
 
• **Lavani**__
 
 
• **Lavani** is a traditional dance form from the state of **Maharashtra**, performed to the beats of **dholki** (a percussion instrument).
 
• It is known for its **expressive gestures, fast-paced rhythm, and sensuous movements**.
 
• Lavani plays a significant role in **Maharashtrian folk theatre** and is often performed to narrate stories or social themes.

questions.question: While learning to cook, Rajesh noticed that when he crushed a dozen of groundnuts in a grinder, it gets lined with oil. Whereas no oil is released when he grinds a bowl of cumin. What could be the reason behind this difference?

options.text: The fat in groundnut releases oil.
The protein in groundnut releases oil.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**The fat in groundnut releases oil.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Groundnuts** are rich in **fat content**, specifically natural oils.
 
• When groundnuts are crushed in a grinder, the **mechanical pressure** causes the natural fats to release as oil.
 
• This oil lining can be observed on the walls of the grinder due to the **high oil concentration** in groundnuts.
 
• In contrast, **cumin seeds** have a significantly lower fat content, which is why no oil is released when they are ground.
 
• The difference lies in the **chemical composition** of groundnuts and cumin. Groundnuts are a source of edible oil, while cumin seeds are primarily used for their **aromatic compounds**.
 
• This phenomenon is a direct result of the **oil extraction process**, which is naturally triggered by grinding high-fat content foods like groundnuts.
 
• Understanding this difference is crucial in cooking and food processing, as it explains why some ingredients release oil when processed, while others do not.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Cumin was of bad quality**__

 __
 
• The quality of cumin does not determine whether oil will be released during grinding. The absence of oil release is due to the **low fat content** in cumin, not its quality.
 
 
 
• **The protein in groundnut releases oil**__
 __
 
• Proteins do not release oil. Oils are derived from the **fat content**, not proteins, as proteins are primarily involved in structural and metabolic functions in food.
 
 
 
• **The groundnut was not dried**__
 
 
• Drying affects moisture levels but does not impact the **oil release** significantly. The release of oil is primarily due to the high fat content in groundnuts, not their drying state.

questions.question: Sukta was known as the hymns of which of the following Vedic books?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rigveda**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sukta** refers to the **hymns or mantras** that are part of the **Rigveda**.
 
• The **Rigveda** is the **oldest Vedic text** and one of the most important scriptures of ancient Indian literature.
 
• It consists of **1028 hymns (Suktas)**, divided into **10 mandalas (books).**
 
• The hymns are primarily dedicated to various **deities such as Agni, Indra, Varuna, and Soma**.
 
• The **Rigveda** provides insights into the **social, religious, and economic conditions** of the early Vedic period.
 
• The hymns were composed in **Vedic Sanskrit** and were orally transmitted for centuries before being written down.
 
• The focus of the hymns is on **invoking divine forces** for blessings, prosperity, and protection.
 
• The **Rigveda** is considered the foundation of the other three Vedas: **Samaveda, Yajurveda, and Atharvaveda**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Atharvaveda**__

 __
 
• The **Atharvaveda** is the fourth Veda and contains hymns, spells, and incantations for **practical purposes such as healing, protection, and success in life.**
 
• It focuses on **everyday life** and includes topics such as **medicine, rituals, and magic.**
 
 
 
• **Samaveda**__
 __
 
• The **Samaveda** consists of hymns from the **Rigveda**, but they are set to **musical notations** and are meant to be sung during **rituals and sacrifices.**
 
• It is often referred to as the **"Veda of Melodies."**
 
 
 
• **Yajurveda**__
 
 
• The **Yajurveda** contains hymns and mantras necessary for performing **Vedic rituals and sacrifices.**
 
• It is divided into two main categories: **Shukla (White) Yajurveda** and **Krishna (Black) Yajurveda.**

questions.question: What role do MNCs play in the globalisation process?

options.text: They integrate production and markets across different countries.
They regulate national policies on trade.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**They integrate production and markets across different countries.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Multinational Corporations (MNCs)** play a significant role in the **globalisation process** by integrating **production** and **markets** across various countries.
 
• MNCs establish **production units** in multiple countries, enabling the creation of **global supply chains** that connect diverse economies.
 
• They facilitate the flow of **capital, technology, goods, and services**, enhancing economic interdependence among nations.
 
• By investing in different countries, MNCs bring in **foreign direct investment (FDI)**, which contributes to the economic development of host countries.
 
• MNCs often encourage **technological innovation** and the adoption of best practices, improving the efficiency and competitiveness of local industries.
 
• They enable access to **global markets**, helping businesses in host countries expand their operations and reach a larger audience.
 
• MNCs create **employment opportunities** in host countries by setting up new factories, offices, and subsidiaries.
 
• Their operations promote **cultural exchange** and the sharing of ideas, fostering a more interconnected world.
 
• Globalisation through MNCs has led to the availability of **diverse products** and services in international markets, enriching consumer choices.
 
• Examples of prominent MNCs include **Apple, Microsoft, Coca-Cola, and Toyota**, which operate across multiple countries and contribute to global interconnectedness.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **They regulate national policies on trade.**__

 __
 
• MNCs do not have the authority to directly regulate **national trade policies**. This responsibility lies with governments and international organisations such as the **World Trade Organization (WTO).**
 
• While MNCs may influence trade policies indirectly through lobbying or economic impact, they do not possess regulatory power.
 
 
 
• **They promote local businesses only.**__
 __
 
• MNCs do not exclusively promote **local businesses**. Instead, they operate globally, often competing with local businesses or collaborating with them for mutual benefit.
 
• In some cases, MNCs may overshadow local businesses due to their larger scale and resources.
 
 
 
• **They discourage international trade.**__
 
 
• MNCs do not discourage **international trade**; rather, they facilitate it by creating cross-border supply chains and expanding global markets.
 
• They promote trade by connecting producers and consumers across different countries.

questions.question: The 'August Offer' of 1940 was made by which British government official?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Linlithgow**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **‘August Offer’** was made by **Lord Linlithgow**, the then **Viceroy of India**, in **August 1940**.
 
• The offer was an attempt by the British government to secure Indian support during **World War II**.
 
• It promised to grant **Dominion Status** to India after the war.
 
• It also proposed to expand the **Executive Council of the Viceroy**, including more Indian members.
 
• The British government assured that a **Constituent Assembly** would be formed to frame the future Constitution of India, with provisions for minorities' consent.
 
• The **Indian National Congress** rejected the offer as it fell short of their demand for complete independence.
 
• The **Muslim League** found the offer insufficient and continued to press for the creation of **Pakistan**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Neville Chamberlain**__

 __
 
• **Neville Chamberlain** was the **Prime Minister of the United Kingdom** from **1937 to 1940**.
 
• He is best known for his policy of **appeasement** towards Nazi Germany, particularly for signing the **Munich Agreement** in 1938.
 
• Chamberlain resigned in May 1940, succeeded by Winston Churchill.
 
 
 
• **Clement Attlee**__
 __
 
• **Clement Attlee** was the **Prime Minister of the United Kingdom** from **1945 to 1951**.
 
• He played a crucial role in granting **independence to India** in **1947**.
 
• His government also established the **National Health Service (NHS)** in the UK.
 
 
 
• **Winston Churchill**__
 
 
• **Winston Churchill** was the **Prime Minister of the United Kingdom** during **World War II**, serving from **1940 to 1945** and again from **1951 to 1955**.
 
• Churchill was known for his strong opposition to granting independence to India and referred to **Mahatma Gandhi** in derogatory terms.
 
• His leadership during the war earned him widespread recognition as a wartime leader.

questions.question: In which type of climate are deciduous forests and tree-shredded grasslands found?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Tropical wet and dry climate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Deciduous forests and tree-shredded grasslands are typically found in regions with a **Tropical wet and dry climate**, also known as the **Savanna climate**.
 
• This climate is characterized by **distinct wet and dry seasons**, which influence vegetation patterns.
 
• The presence of a **long dry season** causes trees to shed their leaves to conserve water, forming deciduous forests.
 
• Tree-shredded grasslands are a common feature, where grasses dominate the landscape alongside scattered trees.
 
• This type of climate is usually found between **tropical rainforest zones** and **semi-arid regions**.
 
• Regions with a tropical wet and dry climate include parts of **India, Africa, South America, and Australia**.
 
• The climate supports a unique biodiversity, including species adapted to periodic droughts and seasonal rainfall.
 
• The soil in these regions is typically **fertile but prone to erosion** during heavy rains.
 
• Human activities like **agriculture** and **livestock grazing** are significant in these areas due to the vegetation patterns.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Humid subtropical climate**__

 __
 
• This climate is characterized by **hot and humid summers** and **mild winters**.
 
• It is found in regions such as **Southeastern United States, parts of China, Japan, and India**.
 
• The vegetation includes **mixed forests** and is not dominated by deciduous forests or grasslands like in the tropical wet and dry climate.
 
 
 
• **Subtropical steppe climate**__
 __
 
• This climate is semi-arid, with **low rainfall** and high temperatures.
 
• Vegetation consists of **shrubs and grasses**, but lacks dense forests.
 
• Regions with this climate include parts of **Central Asia, Southwestern United States, and Australia**.
 
 
 
• **Warm temperate (mid-latitude) climate**__
 
 
• This climate is found in regions with **moderate temperatures** and **seasonal rainfall**.
 
• Vegetation includes **mixed forests and grasslands**, but it does not exhibit the distinct characteristics of tropical wet and dry climates.
 
• Examples of regions with this climate include **Mediterranean countries** and parts of **California**.

questions.question: Which of the following is the festival that celebrates Marathi New Year?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Gudi Padwa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gudi Padwa** marks the beginning of the **Marathi New Year**.
 
• It is celebrated on the first day of the **Chaitra month** (March-April) as per the **Hindu lunar calendar.**
 
• The festival is mainly observed in the state of **Maharashtra** and some parts of **Goa.**
 
• On this day, a **Gudi** (a bright yellow or saffron cloth adorned with garlands) is hoisted on a bamboo stick, symbolizing **prosperity and victory.**
 
• The festival holds religious and cultural importance as it is also believed to mark the day when **Brahma created the universe.**
 
• Traditional food items like **Puran Poli** and **Shrikhand** are prepared and enjoyed during the celebration.
 
• It is considered an auspicious day for starting new ventures or undertakings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Makar Sankranti**__

 __
 
• **Makar Sankranti** is a harvest festival celebrated across India in the month of January.
 
• It marks the transition of the Sun into the **Capricorn zodiac sign (Makara Rashi)**.
 
• This festival is associated with **kite flying, sesame sweets (tilgul),** and prayers to the Sun God.
 
 
 
• **Ugadi**__
 __
 
• **Ugadi** is celebrated as the **New Year** in the states of **Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh,** and **Telangana.**
 
• It is observed on the first day of the **Chaitra month** as per the Hindu lunar calendar.
 
• The festival involves the preparation of a special dish called **Ugadi Pachadi**, which symbolizes different emotions of life.
 
 
 
• **Pongal**__
 
 
• **Pongal** is a harvest festival celebrated primarily in the state of **Tamil Nadu.**
 
• It is observed in the month of **January** and marks the beginning of the Sun's northward journey (Uttarayan).
 
• A special dish called **Pongal** is prepared using rice, milk, and jaggery during the festival.

questions.question: The focus areas of the first and second five-year plans were:
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Agriculture and Industry sectors**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **First Five-Year Plan (1951-1956)** in India focused on **agriculture and irrigation development** as the main priority. It was designed with an emphasis on **agricultural production** to address food shortages.
 
• This plan was heavily influenced by the **Harrod-Domar model**, which emphasizes the role of investment and savings in economic growth.
 
• The First Plan allocated **44.6% of its total budget** to agriculture, irrigation, and community development.
 
• The **Second Five-Year Plan (1956-1961)** shifted focus toward the **industrial sector**. It aimed to establish a strong industrial base, particularly in heavy industries such as steel and machinery.
 
• The Second Plan was based on the **Mahalanobis model**, which advocated for rapid industrialization and a focus on capital goods.
 
• Key projects under these plans included the establishment of major dams like **Bhakra Nangal** (First Plan) and the expansion of industries like **Bhilai Steel Plant** (Second Plan).
 
• The combined focus on **Agriculture** in the First Plan and **Industry** in the Second Plan laid the foundation for India's socio-economic development.
 
• These plans were significant in addressing India's **food security** challenges and creating infrastructure for long-term industrial growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Industry and Service Sectors**__

 __
 
• This option is incorrect because the focus on **service sectors** did not emerge strongly in the early Five-Year Plans. Services became more prominent in later plans as the economy diversified.
 
• While industrial development was a focus in the Second Plan, the service sector was not prioritized during the initial plans.
 
 
 
• **Agriculture and Service Sectors**__
 __
 
• This option is incorrect as the **First Plan** focused primarily on agriculture, but the service sector was not emphasized during the first two plans.
 
• Service sectors gained importance in later decades when the Indian economy transitioned towards a more service-driven model.
 
 
 
• **Agriculture and Foreign Sectors**__
 
 
• The foreign sector was not a direct focus in the early Five-Year Plans. The emphasis was on **domestic development**, including agriculture and industry.
 
• India's foreign trade and external sectors were addressed in later plans as globalization and liberalization policies emerged.

questions.question: Vacation, resignation and removal from the offices of Speaker and Deputy Speaker are addressed in which Article of the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Article 94**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 94** of the **Indian Constitution** deals with the **vacation, resignation, and removal** from the offices of the **Speaker and Deputy Speaker** of the **House of the People (Lok Sabha).**
 
• According to this article, the **Speaker or Deputy Speaker** must vacate their office in the following cases:
 
 
• When they cease to be a member of the **House of the People**.
 
• When they resign from their position by submitting a letter to another presiding officer.
 
• When they are removed from office by a resolution passed by a majority of all the members of the **Lok Sabha**.
 
 
 
• The resolution for removal requires a **14-day notice** before being moved in the House.
 
• This article ensures the accountability and proper functioning of the offices of the **Speaker and Deputy Speaker** in India's parliamentary system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 70**__

 __
 
• **Article 70** of the **Indian Constitution** deals with the discharge of the functions of the **President** in certain contingencies.
 
• It empowers Parliament to make laws regarding how the functions of the President will be discharged in case of a vacancy in the office or if the President is unable to perform duties due to absence, illness, or any other reason.
 
 
 
• **Article 101**__
 __
 
• **Article 101** lays down provisions regarding the **vacation of seats**, disqualifications, and **dual membership** in the Parliament.
 
• It prevents a person from being a member of both Houses of Parliament at the same time and addresses conditions for vacating a seat.
 
 
 
• **Article 84**__
 
 
• **Article 84** specifies the **qualifications** required to be elected as a member of **Parliament**.
 
• These include being a citizen of India, meeting the minimum age requirement, and other criteria prescribed by law.
